answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every identity must climb a reputation ridge one verified step at a time: each completed job earns a signed receipt chained to the last, and the chain is published in a shared atlas of attestations any peer can audit. A fresh account starts with no credit and cannot buy its way up; one forged receipt breaks the chain and slashes the locked stake. A gale of a thousand fake identities therefore costs a thousand deposits and a thousand jobs, so forgery pays less than honest work.
